title: Alberta Serious Incident Response Team clears Vegreville Mountie in fatal shooting of Russell Skoropad
article: The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) has cleared a Vegreville Mountie who fatally shot a 43-year-old man at a rural property last year.
Around 2:10 p.m. on July 18, 2012, a minor dispute between family members at a property near the junction of Highway 36 and Highway 631 triggered a call to 911.

Officers from the Vegreville and Two Hills RCMP detachment responded to the call that indicated the man -- Russell Skoropad -- was breaching a recognizance by drinking and entering the main residence on the property.

Before officers arrived at the scene, a second call was placed to 911, altering officials that Skoropad was in possession of a shotgun outside of the main residence, where his two brothers and mother were inside.
Two officers entered the residence to provide protection to the family, while a third officer took position outside of the home.

According to Jane McClellan, acting executive director of ASIRT, the two members inside the home made numerous attempts to communicate with Skoropad and have him put down the loaded shotgun. But he was highly intoxicated, and threatened to shoot anyone on the property.

At one point, Skoropad fired a shot into the air when he was in some trees away from the home. Eventually he walked towards the main residence, then changed his course and headed towards the third police officer outside.
The officer announced his presence and ordered Skoropad to drop his weapon. But he didn't listen, and advanced further towards the officer.

"The officer at that stage believed that he would be shot and killed or grievously injured if he did not discharge his weapon," said McClellan, adding Skoropad was three times the legal alcohol limit.
The officer fired his weapon, striking Skoropad in the chest. Despite the efforts of paramedics, he was pronounced dead at the scene. A total of 12 shotgun shells were found in his possession.

At no point did Skoropad point his gun at the officer, but McClellan said he held it in his hand with the barrel resting on his shoulder. A use of force expert in the case concluded that the amount of time it would take to move the gun to a firing position would be a fraction of a second.
"He was a lethal threat to that third officer," said McClellan.
Skoropad was the youngest of three brothers who lived on the property with their mother. An area resident said the brothers had problems getting along.

The shooting marks the second time RCMP in Vegreville have fatally shot a man. In July 2008, an armed Leo Raymond Poulin was shot and killed in a parking lot. No criminal charges were laid against the officer who fired the three fatal shots.
